title: story new --help creates a story titled "--help" instead of printing help

description:
## What

`story new --help` does not print help. It creates a real story whose title is the literal string `--help`, allocating an ID and incrementing `next-id`.

## Repro

    $ story new --help
    SH-48 --help
    state: todo (OPEN)
    assignee: -
    priority: none
    type: Default

Observed directly while working on the v0.17.0 release; it burned SH-48 in a local tree and had to be manually deleted plus `next-id` reverted.

## Why it breaks

`story new <title>` takes the first positional argument as the title with no flag handling ahead of it, so any `--`-prefixed token in the title position is swallowed as content rather than parsed as a flag.

## Extent

- Any `story <verb> --help` that takes a positional is suspect; `new` is confirmed. Sweep the other positional-taking verbs (`search`, `phase create`, `member add`, `import`, `decompose`, `web register`) before closing.
- The damage is silent and persistent: it writes a story file, mutates `next-id`, and (in a storyhook-tracked repo) leaves the tree dirty. A user probing for usage gets a junk story instead of an error.
- `--help` is the conventional discovery gesture, so this is likely to be hit by exactly the users who least expect it.

## Last known good

Unknown; likely present since `story new` gained positional-title parsing.

## Fix

Handle `-h`/`--help` (and reject unknown leading `--` tokens) before positional-title parsing, for every verb that takes a positional. Preventative action: a table-driven test asserting that `<verb> --help` exits 0, prints usage, and mutates no state, run across the full verb list so the class cannot regress one verb at a time.
